title: What is the difference between the Factory and Abstract Factory patterns?
shortTitle: What is the difference between the Factory and Abstract Factory patterns
keyPoints: Factory produces one product from one hierarchy; Abstract Factory produces a matching family of products.
Factory answers "which one concrete class?"; Abstract Factory answers "which consistent set of classes?"
Abstract Factory has a factory interface with one method per product; each concrete factory produces a matching family.
Swapping the Abstract Factory swaps the entire family at once, keeping products consistent.
Use Factory for one product whose type varies; use Abstract Factory when products must stay consistent as a set.
Abstract Factory has more machinery; only use it when family consistency genuinely matters.

s1_definition.oneliner: Factory produces one product; Abstract Factory produces a whole matching family of products through a factory of factories.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Factory (Factory Method)** – creates a single product from one hierarchy by choosing the concrete class behind a method.
- **Abstract Factory** – creates families of related products that are designed to be used together; each concrete factory produces one complete, consistent family.
- **Key difference** – Factory decides one product; Abstract Factory decides a matching set and guarantees they belong together.
- **Swapping** – swapping an Abstract Factory swaps the entire family at once.
- **Guidance** – use Abstract Factory only when product consistency genuinely matters.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, the Factory is the single counter that hands Rajesh the one thing he asked for, such as a savings-account kit. The Abstract Factory is the regional branch office that hands him a whole matched set for his region: the regional form, the regional card design, and the regional cheque book, all guaranteed to belong to the same region.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Factory vs Abstract Factory
  ───────────────────────────

  Factory (one product):
  Client ──▶ ProcessorFactory.create("UPI") ──▶ UpiProcessor

  Abstract Factory (matching family):
  Client ──▶ RegulatoryDocFactory
                  │
                  ├──▶ createHeader()    ──▶ RegulatoryHeader
                  ├──▶ createFormatter() ──▶ RegulatoryFormatter
                  └──▶ createFooter()    ──▶ RegulatoryFooter

  Swap factory ──▶ CustomerDocFactory
                  │
                  ├──▶ createHeader()    ──▶ CustomerHeader
                  ├──▶ createFormatter() ──▶ CustomerFormatter
                  └──▶ createFooter()    ──▶ CustomerFooter

  Entire family swaps together – consistency guaranteed
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The difference comes down to how many products the pattern creates and whether they must be consistent. Factory creates a single product from one hierarchy: it hides `new` behind a method and decides which concrete class. Abstract Factory creates a whole family of related products through a factory interface whose implementations each produce one complete, consistent set.

At National Bank of India, when a trade arrives and Pankaj needs the one correct settlement handler, that is a single-product decision and a plain Factory is enough. But when generating documents, a regulatory filing needs a regulatory header, a regulatory formatter, and a regulatory footer. Mixing a customer header with a regulatory formatter would produce an invalid document. That consistency requirement is exactly why the Abstract Factory exists.

The client depends only on the abstract factory and product interfaces. Rajesh's report-generation code takes a `DocumentFactory` and calls `createHeader`, `createFormatter`, and `createFooter`. Switching the entire family is a one-line change: hand it a different factory, and all products switch together.

The senior judgment is that Abstract Factory has more machinery, so Pankaj only uses it when family consistency genuinely matters. If products do not need to match, separate factory methods are simpler.

Remember one sentence: Factory picks one concrete product, Abstract Factory picks a matching family where all products must be consistent.
